name.text: 16.1 Q5 Farmers and cooperative societies in Meru

questiontext.text:
[[if test="is(ctx=1)"]]

Coffee farmers in Meru each register with exactly one cooperative society. There are about {@nf@} farmers and {@nc@} cooperative societies. Each society processes coffee from many farmers, but each farmer belongs to only one society.

The input is the farmer and the output is the cooperative society.

[[else]]

Farmers from four villages near Kericho, namely Kapsoit, Chilchila, Kabianga and Ainamoi, all deliver their tea leaves to the same collection centre in Kericho town.

The input is the village and the output is the collection centre.

[[/if]]

(a) What type of relation is this?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Choose the statement that correctly explains whether this relation is a function.

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
[[if test="is(ctx=1)"]]

The input is the farmer and the output is the cooperative society. Each farmer has exactly one society, and many farmers share the same society. Many inputs go to one output, so the relation is many-to-one.

[[else]]

The input is the village and the output is the collection centre. Each village delivers to exactly one centre, and all four villages share the same centre. Many inputs go to one output, so the relation is many-to-one. It is not one-to-one, because the villages share a centre, and it is not one-to-many, because no village delivers to two centres.

[[/if]]

A relation is a function when every input has exactly one output. That is true here, so the relation is a function. Many inputs sharing one output is allowed for a function; a function need not be one-to-one.

questionnote.text: [[if test="is(ctx=1)"]]Meru coffee, nf={@nf@}, nc={@nc@}[[else]]Kericho tea villages[[/if]]; many-to-one, a function

questiondescription.text: This question is based on the definitions of one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many relations in Section 16.1 (Types of Relations) of the Grade 11 Functions topic. It merges the former Relations Q6 (Kericho tea villages and one collection centre) into this question as a second context.

truefeedback.text: It looks like you read the relation backwards, treating the output as the input. The question names the input and the output. Start from one input and count how many outputs it has, then ask whether several inputs share an output.

falsefeedback.text: Check both directions. Does any single input have more than one output? Do several inputs share the same output? The type is named inputs-to-outputs.

Recall the definition: a relation is a function when every input has exactly one output. Check whether that holds here. Several inputs sharing an output is allowed, and a function does not have to be one-to-one.
